note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count and address below comes from one City of St. George page, its Pickleball page, where a four-line list headed "City of St. George Pickleball Courts" gives each venue a name, a street address and a court count. The same page carries the City's 2025 programme schedule for Little Valley, a check-in rule, and an article dated 19 August 2020 that is used here for history and nothing else. Where the City is silent, on lighting, surface, hours and parking at every venue, and on price at two of the three, this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking:
St. George publishes nothing about parking at any of these three venues. The word does not appear in the City's four-line court list, which gives each venue a name, a street address and a count and nothing more. Nothing is said about restrooms at any venue either.

The scale makes that a real gap: two tournaments a year take "All 33 Courts" at Little Valley from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.

What the City does state about arriving is a rule rather than a lot. At Little Valley, "Players, please check in with the attendant or instructor to determine if courts are available during the St. George Pickleball programs".
slots.peak_hours:
The City publishes no opening hours and no closing time for any of its pickleball courts, and for Vernon Worthen Park and Bloomington Park it publishes nothing about timing at all.

For Little Valley it publishes a full programme schedule, headed "St. George Pickleball Program Schedule / 2025", which says which courts are reserved, when, and for what. Winter League runs from 6 January to early March on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday mornings from 9:30 to 11:30 a.m. and evenings from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m., with Wednesday evenings running to 9:30, and each session reserves "9-32 (24 courts)". Spring League repeats the pattern from 24 March into May. Two tournaments take everything: the Rock N Roll Tournament, 6 to 8 February, and the Southern Shootout, 2 to 5 April, each "All 33 Courts".

So a league session leaves nine courts unreserved and a tournament leaves none. The City adds that "Times may change based on participation numbers".
slots.surface_condition:
The City names no surface anywhere on its pickleball page. The court list gives a name, an address and a count per venue, and the only descriptive words about the courts are in the 2020 article, which calls Little Valley "home to 24 well-maintained courts". That is about upkeep in 2020, not about what the courts are made of.

What the City does make clear is what kind of place each venue is. Little Valley carries a schedule that numbers its courts from 1 to 33, reserves them in blocks, and books all thirty-three for tournaments. A place whose courts have numbers on a timetable is a pickleball facility rather than a park with lines painted on something else, and it is published here as a dedicated pickleball facility. Vernon Worthen and Bloomington are published as parks; how their courts are laid out is not stated, and nothing is stated about whether any court in the city is indoor, outdoor or covered.
slots.local_scene:
Forty-six courts across three City venues. St. George is the first Utah city on this site and the first in Washington County, and it arrives with a venue that ties for the largest single count anywhere here: Little Valley Pickleball Complex's thirty-three.

The City's page is unlike most on this site because it is a programme page rather than an inventory. It lists leagues, academies, clinics and tournaments under a Tennis and Pickleball Head Pro, Wayne P. Bullock. Its 2020 article says that in 2012 Bullock "established the first pickleball program for the City of St. George on four permanent and two temporary courts at Vernon Worthen Park".

One venue is refused: the City's list reads "Ledges / ? / Courts: 4", a question mark where the address should be. Price is stated once, in the 2020 article, and only for Little Valley, where when courts are vacant "the public readily takes advantage of them", "free of charge". Vernon Worthen and Bloomington carry no price, no hours, no lighting and no surface.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts in one place
best_for.text: Little Valley Pickleball Complex has thirty-three courts, the largest count in Utah on this site and tied for the largest anywhere here. It is a programmed facility: the City reserves courts for leagues, clinics and tournaments on a published schedule, an attendant tells you what is free, and the City states that vacant courts are free of charge. Hours, lighting and surface are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to play where the programme began
best_for.text: Vernon Worthen Park is where the City's pickleball programme began in 2012, on "four permanent and two temporary courts" in the City's own words, and where the ladder-league format later adopted by USA Pickleball was launched. Six courts today at a Utah grid address, 300 S. 400 E., near the centre of the city. Price, hours, lighting and surface are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want courts with no timetable attached
best_for.text: Bloomington Park has seven courts and none of the apparatus of Little Valley: no published schedule, no reserved blocks, no attendant to check in with. The City states the name, the address and the count and nothing else, so what you get is seven courts in the south-west of the city with the price, hours, lighting and surface unstated. Seven courts is seven games at once.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does St. George have?
faqs.a: Forty-six across three City venues, all stated on one page: thirty-three at Little Valley Pickleball Complex, seven at Bloomington Park and six at Vernon Worthen Park. The City also lists Ledges with four courts and prints "?" where its address should be, so it is not published.

faqs.q: Which St. George courts have lights?
faqs.a: Not stated at any venue. The City never uses the word on its pickleball page, and this site publishes lighting only when the operator writes it. Little Valley's schedule runs league sessions until 8:30 and 9:30 p.m. in January, which is a fact about the timetable and not a statement about lamps.

sources.evidence: The City's Pickleball page. Under "City of St. George Pickleball Courts" exactly four lines: "Little Valley / 2149 Horseman Park Drive / Courts:  33", "Vernon Worthen / 300 S. 400 E. / Courts: 6", "Bloomington Park / 650 Man O War Road / Courts: 7", "Ledges / ? / Courts: 4". The check-in rule: "Players, please check in with the attendant or instructor to determine if courts are available during the St. George Pickleball programs". The "St. George Pickleball Program Schedule / 2025" for Little Valley reserves "9-32 (24 courts)" for Winter and Spring League sessions (mornings 9:30-11:30 a.m. in winter and 9:00-11:00 a.m. in spring, evenings 6:30-8:30 p.m., Wednesdays 6:30-9:30 p.m.), "21-22, 26-29 (6 courts)" for youth sessions 4:00-7:00 p.m., "27-28 (2 courts)" for adult clinics, and "All 33 Courts" from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. for the Rock N Roll Tournament (6-8 February) and the Southern Shootout (2-5 April); "Times may change based on participation numbers". The article dated "St. George, UT, August 19, 2020": "the Little Valley Pickleball Complex in St. George, UT was chosen as \"Public Facility of the Year\" by the PPR"; "In 2012, Wayne Bullock established the first pickleball program for the City of St. George on four permanent and two temporary courts at Vernon Worthen Park"; "the USA Pickleball Association contacted Bullock for permission to adopt it"; "The Little Valley Pickleball complex is home to 24 well-maintained courts."; "When courts are vacant the public readily takes advantage of them - free of charge."; "The growth of the programs aids in maintaining the courts, which fortifies the cleanliness of the facility for the public." Also "Please report non-city / unauthorized clinics, lessons, tournaments, or camps to the Parks Department at 435-627-4530", "Please contact Parks to make a court reservation at 435-627-4530", "Non-City events are required to have a court reservation and possibly a special event permit.", a "Reserve a Pickleball Court" link, and the Tennis & Pickleball Head Pro "Wayne P. Bullock (435) 627-4522". Snapshot: data/sources/st-george/pickleball.html
